sanskrit: tam apsarogaṇākīrṇaṃ gītasvananināditam kiṃnarāṇāṃ samūhaiś ca bhṛṅgarājais tathaiva ca
english: That mountain was thronged with troops of apsarases and resounded with the strains of song; it teemed with bands of kiṃnaras and with kingfishers as well,

sanskrit: madgubhiḥ khañjarīṭaiś ca vicitrair jīvajīvakaiḥ citravarṇair mayūraiś ca kekāśatavirājitaiḥ rājahaṃsasamūhaiś ca hṛṣṭaiḥ parabhṛtais tathā
english: with cormorants and wagtails, with bright-hued jīvajīvaka birds, with peacocks of brilliant plumage radiant with a hundred cries, with flocks of royal swans, and with joyous cuckoos.

sanskrit: pakṣirājo garutmāṃś ca yaṃ nityam adhigacchati catvāro lokapālāś ca devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tathā yatra nityaṃ samāyānti lokasya hitakāmyayā
english: There the king of birds, Garutmān, comes ever and again; and there the four guardians of the world, the gods together with their hosts of sages, repair continually, desiring the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā yatra putrārthe tapas taptaṃ mahātmanā yatraiva ca kumāreṇa bālye kṣiptā divaukasaḥ
english: There the great-souled Viṣṇu once performed austerities for the sake of a son; and there in his childhood Kumāra hurled defiance at the dwellers in heaven,

sanskrit: śaktir nyastā kṣititale trailokyam avamanya vai yatrovāca jagatskandaḥ kṣipan vākyam idaṃ tadā
english: when Skanda, scorning the three worlds, planted his spear upon the surface of the earth, and the lord of the world spoke these challenging words:

sanskrit: yo 'nyo 'sti matto 'bhyadhiko viprā yasyādhikaṃ priyāḥ yo brahmaṇyo dvitīyo 'sti triṣu lokeṣu vīryavān
english: "If there be another mightier than I, O brāhmaṇas, one dearer to you and more devoted to brahman, a second hero of valor in the three worlds—

sanskrit: so 'bhyuddharatv imāṃ śaktim atha vā kampayatv iti tac chrutvā vyathitā lokāḥ ka imām uddhared iti
english: let him lift up this spear, or even make it tremble!" Hearing this, the worlds were thrown into dismay, wondering, "Who could lift this up?"

sanskrit: atha devagaṇaṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhrāntendriyamānasam apaśyad bhagavān viṣṇuḥ kṣiptaṃ sāsurarākṣasam kiṃ nv atra sukṛtaṃ kāryaṃ bhaved iti vicintayan
english: Then the blessed Viṣṇu beheld the whole host of gods, with senses and minds bewildered, dismayed together with the asuras and rākṣasas, and he pondered, "What deed well done would here be fitting?"

sanskrit: sa nāmṛṣyata taṃ kṣepam avaikṣata ca pāvakim sa prahasya viśuddhātmā śaktiṃ prajvalitāṃ tadā kampayām āsa savyena pāṇinā puruṣottamaḥ
english: He would not brook that challenge, and he looked upon the son of Fire. Then the Supreme Person, pure of soul, laughed, and with his left hand made the blazing spear tremble.

sanskrit: śaktyāṃ tu kampamānāyāṃ viṣṇunā balinā tadā medinī kampitā sarvā saśailavanakānanā
english: And when the spear was set trembling by the mighty Viṣṇu, the whole earth was shaken, with its mountains, woods, and forests.

sanskrit: śaktenāpi samuddhartuṃ kampitā sā na tūddhṛtā rakṣatā skandarājasya dharṣaṇāṃ prabhaviṣṇunā
english: Though able to wrench it up, the lord Viṣṇu only made it tremble and did not draw it forth, sparing thereby the glory of King Skanda's challenge.

sanskrit: tāṃ kampayitvā bhagavān prahrādam idam abravīt paśya vīryaṃ kumārasya naitad anyaḥ kariṣyati
english: Having made it tremble, the blessed one said this to Prahrāda: "Behold the valor of Kumāra—no other could do this deed."

sanskrit: so 'mṛṣyamāṇas tad vākyaṃ samuddharaṇaniścitaḥ jagrāha tāṃ tasya śaktiṃ na cainām apy akampayat
english: Unable to bear those words, Prahrāda, resolved to wrench it up, seized the spear of Skanda—yet he could not so much as make it tremble.

sanskrit: nādaṃ mahāntaṃ muktvā sa mūrchito girimūrdhani vihvalaḥ prāpatad bhūmau hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sutaḥ
english: Letting forth a mighty cry, the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, swooning and overcome, fell to the ground upon the summit of the mountain.

sanskrit: yatrottarāṃ diśaṃ gatvā śailarājasya pārśvataḥ tapo 'tapyata durdharṣas tāta nityaṃ vṛṣadhvajaḥ
english: There, my son, having gone to the northern quarter beside the king of mountains, the unassailable god whose banner bears the bull performed his austerities without ceasing.

sanskrit: pāvakena parikṣipto dīpyatā tasya cāśramaḥ ādityabandhanaṃ nāma durdharṣam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: His hermitage was encircled by blazing fire—a place named Ādityabandhana, unapproachable by those who have not subdued themselves.

sanskrit: na tatra śakyate gantuṃ yakṣarākṣasadānavaiḥ daśayojanavistāram agnijvālāsamāvṛtam
english: There no yakṣas, rākṣasas, or dānavas can pass; ten yojanas in extent, it is wholly wrapped in flames of fire.

sanskrit: bhagavān pāvakas tatra svayaṃ tiṣṭhati vīryavān sarvavighnān praśamayan mahādevasya dhīmataḥ
english: There the blessed and valorous Fire-god himself abides, quelling every obstacle for the wise Mahādeva.

sanskrit: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi pādenaikena tiṣṭhataḥ devān saṃtāpayaṃs tatra mahādevo dhṛtavrataḥ
english: For a thousand divine years Mahādeva, firm in his vow, stood there upon a single foot, scorching the gods with the heat of his penance.

sanskrit: aindrīṃ tu diśam āsthāya śailarājasya dhīmataḥ vivikte parvatataṭe pārāśaryo mahātapāḥ vedān adhyāpayām āsa vyāsaḥ śiṣyān mahātapāḥ
english: But upon the eastern quarter of the wise king of mountains, on a secluded slope, the son of Parāśara, the great ascetic Vyāsa, of mighty penance, instructed his disciples in the Vedas.

sanskrit: sumantuṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ vaiśaṃpāyanam eva ca jaiminiṃ ca mahāprājñaṃ pailaṃ cāpi tapasvinam
english: He taught the illustrious Sumantu, and Vaiśaṃpāyana, and the deeply wise Jaimini, and Paila too, the ascetic—

sanskrit: ebhiḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto vyāsa āste mahātapāḥ tatrāśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ dadarśa pitur uttamam āraṇeyo viśuddhātmā nabhasīva divākaraḥ
english: surrounded by these disciples sat Vyāsa of great penance. There the son sprung from the kindling-sticks, pure of soul, beheld his father's holy and excellent hermitage, shining like the sun in the sky.

sanskrit: atha vyāsaḥ parikṣiptaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam dadarśa sutam āyāntaṃ divākarasamaprabham
english: Then Vyāsa beheld his son drawing near—encircled with radiance, blazing like fire, splendid as the sun itself.

sanskrit: asajjamānaṃ vṛkṣeṣu śaileṣu viṣameṣu ca yogayuktaṃ mahātmānaṃ yathā bāṇaṃ guṇacyutam
english: Unimpeded by trees, by crags, or by rugged ground, the great-souled one, yoked in yoga, came like an arrow loosed from the bowstring.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya pituḥ pādāv agṛhṇād araṇīsutaḥ yathopajoṣaṃ taiś cāpi samāgacchan mahāmuniḥ
english: Approaching, the son born of the kindling-sticks clasped his father's feet; and the great sage greeted those disciples too, each according to his pleasure.

sanskrit: tato nivedayām āsa pitre sarvam aśeṣataḥ śuko janakarājena saṃvādaṃ prītamānasaḥ
english: Then Śuka, his heart full of joy, reported to his father in full and without omission his colloquy with King Janaka.

sanskrit: evam adhyāpayañ śiṣyān vyāsaḥ putraṃ ca vīryavān uvāsa himavatpṛṣṭhe pārāśaryo mahāmuniḥ
english: Thus instructing his disciples and his son, the valorous son of Parāśara, the great sage Vyāsa, dwelt upon the flank of the Himavat.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cic chiṣyās taṃ parivāryāvatasthire vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ śāntātmāno jitendriyāḥ
english: Then on a certain day the disciples gathered round him and stood before him—accomplished in the study of the Vedas, tranquil of soul, their senses conquered.

sanskrit: vedeṣu niṣṭhāṃ saṃprāpya sāṅgeṣv atitapasvinaḥ athocus te tadā vyāsaṃ śiṣyāḥ prāñjalayo gurum
english: Having attained mastery in the Vedas with their auxiliary sciences, those disciples of surpassing austerity then spoke to Vyāsa, their teacher, with hands joined in reverence:

sanskrit: mahatā śreyasā yuktā yaśasā ca sma vardhitāḥ ekaṃ tv idānīm icchāmo guruṇānugrahaṃ kṛtam
english: "Blessed with great good fortune and enriched with renown are we; yet now we desire one favor to be granted us by our teacher."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā brahmarṣis tān uvāca ha ucyatām iti tad vatsā yad vaḥ kāryaṃ priyaṃ mayā
english: Hearing their words, the brahmarṣi said to them, "Speak it, my children—whatever you would have done, that is dear to me."

sanskrit: etad vākyaṃ guroḥ śrutvā śiṣyās te hṛṣṭamānasāḥ punaḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā praṇamya śirasā gurum
english: Hearing this word of their teacher, the disciples, glad at heart, again folded their hands and, bowing their heads to their guru,

sanskrit: ūcus te sahitā rājann idaṃ vacanam uttamam yadi prīta upādhyāyo dhanyāḥ smo munisattama
english: spoke together, O king, this excellent word: "If our preceptor is pleased with us, then blessed are we, O best of sages.

sanskrit: kāṅkṣāmas tu vayaṃ sarve varaṃ dattaṃ maharṣiṇā ṣaṣṭhaḥ śiṣyo na te khyātiṃ gacched atra prasīda naḥ
english: We all crave one boon granted by the great sage: that no sixth disciple of yours should attain renown in this lore. Be gracious to us in this."

sanskrit: catvāras te vayaṃ śiṣyā guruputraś ca pañcamaḥ iha vedāḥ pratiṣṭherann eṣa naḥ kāṅkṣito varaḥ
english: "We four are your disciples, and the teacher's son is the fifth; let the Vedas be established here in us alone—this is the boon we crave."

sanskrit: śiṣyāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā vyāso vedārthatattvavit parāśarātmajo dhīmān paralokārthacintakaḥ uvāca śiṣyān dharmātmā dharmyaṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing the disciples' words, Vyāsa, knower of the truth of the Vedas' meaning, the wise son of Parāśara, mindful of the good of the world beyond, righteous of soul, spoke to his disciples a word in accord with dharma and conducing to the highest weal:

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāya sadā deyaṃ brahma śuśrūṣave bhavet brahmaloke nivāsaṃ yo dhruvaṃ samabhikāṅkṣati
english: "The sacred lore must ever be imparted to a brāhmaṇa who is eager to learn, by one who steadfastly desires a dwelling in the world of brahman.

sanskrit: bhavanto bahulāḥ santu vedo vistāryatām ayam nāśiṣye saṃpradātavyo nāvrate nākṛtātmani
english: Let your numbers grow many; let this Veda be spread abroad. Yet it must not be bestowed upon one who is no true disciple, nor upon one without vows, nor upon one whose soul is unperfected.

sanskrit: ete śiṣyaguṇāḥ sarve vijñātavyā yathārthataḥ nāparīkṣitacāritre vidyā deyā kathaṃ cana
english: All these marks of a true disciple are to be known according to their truth; to one whose conduct has not been tested, knowledge must in no wise be given.

sanskrit: yathā hi kanakaṃ śuddhaṃ tāpacchedanigharṣaṇaiḥ parīkṣeta tathā śiṣyān īkṣet kulaguṇādibhiḥ
english: For as pure gold is tested by heating, cutting, and rubbing, so should one examine disciples by their lineage, their virtues, and the rest.

sanskrit: na niyojyāś ca vaḥ śiṣyā aniyoge mahābhaye yathāmati yathāpāṭhaṃ tathā vidyā phaliṣyati
english: And your disciples must not be set to a task that is no fit task and that is fraught with great peril. According to one's understanding and one's recitation, so will the knowledge bear its fruit.

sanskrit: sarvas taratu durgāṇi sarvo bhadrāṇi paśyatu śrāvayec caturo varṇān kṛtvā brāhmaṇam agrataḥ
english: Let every man cross over hardships; let every man behold good fortune. One may cause the four varṇas to hear the lore, placing the brāhmaṇa foremost.

sanskrit: vedasyādhyayanaṃ hīdaṃ tac ca kāryaṃ mahat smṛtam stutyartham iha devānāṃ vedāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā
english: This study of the Veda is indeed a great duty, so it is held; for the praise of the gods were the Vedas created by the Self-Existent.

sanskrit: yo nirvadeta saṃmohād brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam so 'padhyānād brāhmaṇasya parābhūyād asaṃśayam
english: Whoever out of delusion should revile a brāhmaṇa versed to the end in the Vedas, that man, through the brāhmaṇa's ill-wishing, will without doubt come to ruin.

sanskrit: yaś cādharmeṇa vibrūyād yaś cādharmeṇa pṛcchati tayor anyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ vādhigacchati
english: He who expounds against dharma and he who questions against dharma—one or the other of the two perishes, or else incurs enmity.

sanskrit: etad vaḥ sarvam ākhyātaṃ svādhyāyasya vidhiṃ prati upakuryāc ca śiṣyāṇām etac ca hṛdi vo bhavet
english: All this has been declared to you concerning the rule of sacred recitation. One should do good to his disciples, and let this abide within your hearts."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etac chrutvā guror vākyaṃ vyāsaśiṣyā mahaujasaḥ anyonyaṃ hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pariṣasvajire tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing this word of their teacher, the mighty disciples of Vyāsa, glad of heart, then embraced one another.

sanskrit: uktāḥ smo yad bhagavatā tadātvāyatisaṃhitam tan no manasi saṃrūḍhaṃ kariṣyāmas tathā ca tat
english: "What the blessed one has spoken to us, joined to the present and to the future, is firmly rooted in our minds, and we shall do even so."

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ ca sabhājyaivaṃ suprītamanasaḥ punaḥ vijñāpayanti sma guruṃ punar vākyaviśāradāḥ
english: Thus honoring one another, their hearts well pleased, they—skilled in speech—again made their request to their teacher:

sanskrit: śailād asmān mahīṃ gantuṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ no mahāmune vedān anekadhā kartuṃ yadi te rucitaṃ vibho
english: "We desire, O great sage, to go from this mountain down to the earth, to multiply the Vedas in their many forms—if it be your pleasure, O lord."

sanskrit: śiṣyāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā parāśarasutaḥ prabhuḥ pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam
english: Hearing the disciples' words, the lord, the son of Parāśara, then replied with a word joined to dharma and to wealth, and conducing to their good:

sanskrit: kṣitiṃ vā devalokaṃ vā gamyatāṃ yadi rocate apramādaś ca vaḥ kāryo brahma hi pracuracchalam
english: "Go to the earth or to the world of the gods, whichever pleases you; but you must be ever vigilant, for the sacred lore abounds in pitfalls."

sanskrit: te 'nujñātās tataḥ sarve guruṇā satyavādinā jagmuḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā vyāsaṃ mūrdhnābhivādya ca
english: Then all of them, granted leave by their truth-speaking teacher, departed, having circled Vyāsa from the right and saluted him with their heads bowed.

sanskrit: avatīrya mahīṃ te 'tha cāturhotram akalpayan saṃyājayanto viprāṃś ca rājanyāṃś ca viśas tathā
english: Descending to the earth, they then ordained the office of the four priests, conducting sacrifices for brāhmaṇas, for kṣatriyas, and for vaiśyas alike.

sanskrit: pūjyamānā dvijair nityaṃ modamānā gṛhe ratāḥ yājanādhyāpanaratāḥ śrīmanto lokaviśrutāḥ
english: Ever honored by the twice-born, rejoicing and content in the householder's life, devoted to officiating at sacrifice and to teaching, they were prosperous and renowned throughout the world.

sanskrit: avatīrṇeṣu śiṣyeṣu vyāsaḥ putrasahāyavān tūṣṇīṃ dhyānaparo dhīmān ekānte samupāviśat
english: When his disciples had gone down to the earth, the wise Vyāsa, with only his son for company, sat down in solitude, silent and absorbed in meditation.

sanskrit: taṃ dadarśāśramapade nāradaḥ sumahātapāḥ athainam abravīt kāle madhurākṣarayā girā
english: Nārada, of exceeding great penance, beheld him at the hermitage, and in due season addressed him in a voice of honeyed syllables:

sanskrit: bho bho maharṣe vāsiṣṭha brahmaghoṣo na vartate eko dhyānaparas tūṣṇīṃ kim āsse cintayann iva
english: "Ho there, great sage, descendant of Vasiṣṭha! The chant of the Veda is heard no more. Why do you sit alone, silent and absorbed in thought, as though brooding?"

sanskrit: brahmaghoṣair virahitaḥ parvato 'yaṃ na śobhate rajasā tamasā caiva somaḥ sopaplavo yathā
english: "Bereft of the chant of the Veda, this mountain has no splendor, even as the moon, when eclipsed, is dimmed by dust and darkness.

sanskrit: na bhrājate yathāpūrvaṃ niṣādānām ivālayaḥ devarṣigaṇajuṣṭo 'pi vedadhvaninirākṛtaḥ
english: Though frequented by hosts of divine sages, yet emptied of the sound of the Veda, it shines no longer as before, but is like a dwelling-place of niṣādas.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca hi devāś ca gandharvāś ca mahaujasaḥ vimuktā brahmaghoṣeṇa na bhrājante yathā purā
english: And the sages, the gods, and the mighty gandharvas, forsaken by the chant of the Veda, shine not as they did of old."

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt maharṣe yat tvayā proktaṃ vedavādavicakṣaṇa
english: Hearing Nārada's words, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana said: "Great sage, skilled in the discourse of the Veda, what you have spoken—

sanskrit: etan manonukūlaṃ me bhavān arhati bhāṣitum sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca sarvatra ca kutūhalī
english: this is wholly agreeable to my mind, and you are worthy to declare it, being all-knowing, all-seeing, and ever curious in all things.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu yad vṛttaṃ sarvaṃ tava mate sthitam tad ājñāpaya viprarṣe brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Whatever has come to pass in the three worlds rests entire within your knowledge. Command me then, O brāhmaṇa sage; tell me, what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: yan mayā samanuṣṭheyaṃ brahmarṣe tad udāhara viyuktasyeha śiṣyair me nātihṛṣṭam idaṃ manaḥ
english: "Declare, O brahmarṣi, what I am to perform; for parted now from my disciples, my mind here is not greatly glad."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca anāmnāyamalā vedā brāhmaṇasyāvrataṃ malam malaṃ pṛthivyā vāhīkāḥ strīṇāṃ kautūhalaṃ malam
english: Nārada said: The Vedas are sullied by neglect of recitation; the lack of vows is the brāhmaṇa's stain; the Vāhīkas are the stain of the earth, and idle curiosity the stain of women.

sanskrit: adhīyatāṃ bhavān vedān sārdhaṃ putreṇa dhīmatā vidhunvan brahmaghoṣeṇa rakṣobhayakṛtaṃ tamaḥ
english: Let your honor recite the Vedas together with your wise son, dispelling by the chant of the Veda the darkness wrought by the terror of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā vyāsaḥ paramadharmavit tathety uvāca saṃhṛṣṭo vedābhyāse dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing Nārada's words, Vyāsa, supreme knower of dharma, said "So be it," rejoicing, and firm of vow in the practice of the Veda.

sanskrit: śukena saha putreṇa vedābhyāsam athākarot svareṇoccaiḥ sa śaikṣeṇa lokān āpūrayann iva
english: Then with his son Śuka he set about the recitation of the Veda, with a loud voice trained in the science of accent, as though filling the worlds with sound.

sanskrit: tayor abhyasator evaṃ nānādharmapravādinoḥ vāto 'timātraṃ pravavau samudrānilavejitaḥ
english: As the two recited thus, expounding the manifold doctrines of dharma, a wind blew beyond all measure, driven by the gale off the ocean.

sanskrit: tato 'nadhyāya iti taṃ vyāsaḥ putram avārayat śuko vāritamātras tu kautūhalasamanvitaḥ
english: Thereupon Vyāsa checked his son, saying, "This is a time when study must cease." But Śuka, no sooner checked, was filled with curiosity,

sanskrit: apṛcchat pitaraṃ brahman kuto vāyur abhūd ayam ākhyātum arhati bhavān vāyoḥ sarvaṃ viceṣṭitam
english: and asked his father: "O holy one, whence has this wind arisen? Be pleased to tell me all the workings of the wind."

sanskrit: śukasyaitad vacaḥ śrutvā vyāsaḥ paramavismitaḥ anadhyāyanimitte 'sminn idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing this word of Śuka, Vyāsa, exceedingly amazed, spoke this word concerning the occasion of the suspension of study:

sanskrit: divyaṃ te cakṣur utpannaṃ svasthaṃ te nirmalaṃ manaḥ tamasā rajasā cāpi tyaktaḥ sattve vyavasthitaḥ
english: "A divine eye has arisen in you; your mind is steady and unsullied. Free from darkness and from passion, you are established in goodness.

sanskrit: ādarśe svām iva chāyāṃ paśyasy ātmānam ātmanā nyasyātmani svayaṃ vedān buddhyā samanucintaya
english: As one beholds his own reflection in a mirror, so do you behold the Self by the self. Laying the Vedas within yourself, ponder them well with your intellect.

sanskrit: devayānacaro viṣṇoḥ pitṛyānaś ca tāmasaḥ dvāv etau pretya panthānau divaṃ cādhaś ca gacchataḥ
english: The path of the gods belongs to Viṣṇu; the path of the fathers is of the dark quality. These are the two roads beyond death—the one leading upward to heaven, the other downward.

sanskrit: pṛthivyām antarikṣe ca yatra saṃvānti vāyavaḥ saptaite vāyumārgā vai tān nibodhānupūrvaśaḥ
english: Upon the earth and in the firmament, where the winds blow together, there are these seven paths of the wind. Learn them now from me in their order.

sanskrit: tatra devagaṇāḥ sādhyāḥ samabhūvan mahābalāḥ teṣām apy abhavat putraḥ samāno nāma durjayaḥ
english: There the troops of gods, the Sādhyas, came into being, of mighty strength; and their son too was born, Samāna by name, hard to conquer.

sanskrit: udānas tasya putro 'bhūd vyānas tasyābhavat sutaḥ apānaś ca tato jñeyaḥ prāṇaś cāpi tataḥ param
english: Udāna was his son; Vyāna was Udāna's offspring; and after him is to be known Apāna, and Prāṇa beyond him.

sanskrit: anapatyo 'bhavat prāṇo durdharṣaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ pṛthak karmāṇi teṣāṃ tu pravakṣyāmi yathātatham
english: Prāṇa was without offspring, unassailable, the scorcher of foes. But the several functions of these winds I shall now declare to you according to the truth.
